items.title: 유랑 상단
items.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: landscape 16:9 gameplay concept art for a Korean indie web-game design article, one complete playable screen.
Primary request: create an original polished 2D illustrated strategy game interface for "CARAVAN LEDGER". A wandering merchant deck-building delivery game, showing the crucial decision where accepting too much cargo clogs the action-card hand.
Scene and composition: widescreen direct orthographic digital game screenshot, no device or browser frame. The upper two-thirds are a warm parchment countryside map with exactly six distinct little towns connected by clear branching routes; forests and low hills are quiet supporting detail. One tiny merchant wagon marks the current town, and a highlighted path leads toward a nearby destination. Town labels are simply A, B, C, D, E, F.
UI: thin top bar "DAY 3 / 8", coin icon "18", cargo icon "3". Right inset panel "DELIVERY", small ceramic urn icon, "B → E", "12", and an "ACCEPT" button. Bottom hand contains exactly five large readable cards in one row: "MOVE" with two boot icons, "TRADE" with coin icons, then three brown "CARGO" cards with urn, textile, and crate illustrations. Deck and discard stacks flank the row and show "DECK 12" and "DISCARD 4". An unobtrusive small button reads "END DAY". Make the contrast between useful action cards and heavy cargo cards immediately understandable.
Style: charming handcrafted 2D board-game inspired art, refined tiny painted map buildings, crisp restrained UI, warm cream parchment, muted moss green, terracotta, dark ink. Dense enough to be a credible real gameplay screen with ample legibility, no excessive ornament.
Constraints: exact short English labels and numbers only as specified. Clear consistent letterforms, all UI inside safe margins, no Korean text, no logos, no existing game assets or trademarks, no splash screen, no poster, no collage, no physical tabletop photography. Show the active gameplay decision, not marketing art. Landscape 16:9.
items.inspection: Complete 16:9 screen. Six map towns and five-card hand with two action cards and three cargo cards visible. Exact short labels readable.

items.title: 심해 인양
items.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: landscape 16:9 gameplay concept art for an original indie web game design article.
Primary request: make one complete polished direct 2D gameplay screen for "DEEP SALVAGE", a compact underwater push-your-luck chip-drawing strategy game about collecting artifacts and returning with enough oxygen.
Composition: upper-left and center show a side-on deep ocean cross-section as the active board, from a small support boat on the bright surface through six clearly marked depth bands, numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 down the left edge. A charming tiny professional diver in a warm orange suit is currently at band 4, with a gentle glowing dive line tracing the route back to the boat. Three small discoverable ceramic, coin and astrolabe artifacts are placed near deeper ledges, and sparse sea plants establish scale. Bottom two bands are dark navy, upper bands seafoam and teal. A dotted upward route emphasizes the cost of returning.
UI: slim top header "DEEP SALVAGE" and "DIVE 2 / 5". Right side clean instrument panel "OXYGEN 7", clear seven-segment oxygen meter, "RETURN COST 4", "DEPTH 4". Beneath is "CARGO 3 / 5" with exactly five square slots, three containing artifacts and two empty; one occupied slot has a small sealed lock icon. Bottom horizontal tray "DRAWN CHIPS" contains three circular chips with oxygen tank, fin, and cracked tank symbols, with values "+2", "1", "-1". Three large action buttons at bottom right read "DIVE", "SEAL", "RETURN". Return should appear available, not disabled.
Style: handcrafted refined flat 2D indie illustration, strong readable shapes, soft paper texture, midnight blue and teal ocean with muted orange diver and cream UI cards, understated precise sans serif type. Functional real game UI with breathing space, coherent screen.
Constraints: one screen only, 16:9 landscape. Exact short English labels and numbers only as specified, no long text, no Korean, no logos, no borrowed game assets. No promo poster, no collage, no devices, no photoreal render, no dramatic cinematic camera. Make depth versus oxygen and cargo decisions visible.
items.inspection: Final edited 16:9 screen visually verified. OXYGEN 5 agrees with five filled gauge slots, RETURN COST 4 and DEPTH 4 retained. Six depth bands, diver, cargo 3/5, chips, buttons, and overall composition preserved.

Preserve EVERYTHING else, including OXYGEN label, RETURN COST 4, DEPTH 4, CARGO 3 / 5, six depth bands, diver, ocean artwork, chips, all three action buttons, composition, dimensions, texture, and color. Do not alter any other number or text. This surgical correction makes the oxygen number agree with the five filled gauge slots.

items.title: 골목 축제
items.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: original 16:9 landscape 2D indie-game gameplay concept illustration, one complete digital screen for a Korean game-design article.
Primary request: create "ALLEY FESTIVAL", a multiplayer card-drafting neighborhood festival strategy game. Show the choice of placing a new path which will bring visitors to both your rice-cake stall and an opponent's tea shop.
Scene and composition: complete clean orthographic or very slight isometric gameplay board visible in upper left-center, exactly a five by five square grid of 25 tiles with clear edges. Korean neighborhood market festival inspired miniature shops, paper lanterns, warm afternoon. On the shared board are tiny rice-cake stall with obvious stacked rice cakes, tiny tea shop with steaming teapot, dumpling stall, toy booth, open empty paving tiles, and connected walking paths. Ownership appears as simple blue or coral borders around stall tile bases with small matching flag icons. Small visitors follow a clearly visible yellow arrowed route from a gate through the path past a blue rice-cake stall and then a coral tea shop. One empty tile is highlighted with a translucent proposed straight path.
UI: top bar "ALLEY FESTIVAL", "ROUND 4 / 9", three compact player badges with scores "24", "21", "18". Right clean panel "VISITORS" shows three icon rows: teacup, snack, toy, with corresponding visitor icons and numbers "3", "4", "2". Below it a small "PATH PREVIEW" panel uses a small arrow and shows blue "+3" and coral "+2", visualizing shared benefit from this proposed path. Bottom drafting tray titled "CHOOSE 1" shows four clear cards in one row with exact labels "PATH", "TEA", "GUEST", "RICE"; the PATH card is selected. Beside the row two opponent card backs with small checkmarks show simultaneous selection; a clear button "CONFIRM".
Style: polished hand-painted 2D board-game-like illustration, cream panel backgrounds, deep charcoal restrained typography, sage and warm clay market tiles, soft detailed miniature shop artwork, cheerful but sophisticated. Game board and menus readable at laptop size.
Constraints: only the specified short English UI and numbers, no Korean lettering. One usable cohesive game screen, no device frame, no browser frame, no photography, no title poster, no collage, no existing game logos or trademarks. Avoid decorative clutter. 16:9 landscape.
items.inspection: Complete 16:9 screen. 5x5 neighborhood grid, ownership flags, shared route, draft selection, and opponents ready status visible. Short English labels readable.
